Let \(q=1-p\). By symmetry, assume the first jump is to \(+1\). Define:
- \(A_k\): probability to hit \(0\) from position \(k\) with previous jump away from \(0\);
- \(B_k\): probability to hit \(0\) from position \(k\) with previous jump toward \(0\).

For \(k\ge 2\),
\[
A_k=pA_{k+1}+qB_{k-1},\qquad B_k=pB_{k-1}+qA_{k+1}.
\]
The boundary conditions are
\[
A_1=pA_2+q,\qquad B_1=p+qA_2.
\]

From \(A_k=pA_{k+1}+qB_{k-1}\), we get
\[
B_{k-1}=\frac{A_k-pA_{k+1}}{q}.
\]
Substitute into the second recurrence to obtain
\[
A_{k+2}-2A_{k+1}+A_k=0,
\]
so \(A_k=\alpha+\beta k\) for \(k\ge2\). Since probabilities are bounded, \(\beta=0\), hence \(A_k=c\) for all \(k\ge2\).

Then
\[
B_1=\frac{A_2-pA_3}{q}=c.
\]
But also \(B_1=p+qA_2=p+qc\). Thus
\[
c=p+qc \implies cp=p \implies c=1
\]
for \(0<p<1\). Therefore
\[
A_1=pA_2+q=p+q=1.
\]
If \(p=0\), the flea alternates directions and returns with probability \(1\). If \(p=1\), it never changes direction and never returns.

\[
\boxed{
\begin{cases}
1, & 0\le p<1,\\
0, & p=1.
\end{cases}}
\]
